findings.title: Client role-mapping checks drop built-in admin-role grants
findings.body: This override authorizes role mapping only through the V2 permission schema, unlike `canManage(ClientModel)`, which also honors `MANAGE_CLIENTS`. As a result, an administrator whose access comes from the built-in `MANAGE_CLIENTS` role can manage a client but may be denied when assigning client roles or composites through the corresponding mapping checks. The same omission appears in `canMapCompositeRoles` and `canMapClientScopeRoles`; preserve the existing built-in role grants in these overrides.

findings.title: Client permission enumeration does not return granted client IDs
findings.body: This scans only resources with type `Clients` and adds each matching resource's name to the result. The schema initializes that type on the aggregate all-clients resource, whose name is the literal `Clients`; per-client resources are created separately with the client ID as their name. Consequently, individual grants are not enumerated here, and an all-clients grant adds `Clients` rather than the IDs of the clients it covers. Consumers using this method to filter or enumerate accessible clients will omit authorized clients or receive a non-client identifier.

findings.title: V2 client deletion leaves authorization resources orphaned
findings.body: The removal-event listener now runs only when the legacy `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature is enabled. In a V2-only deployment, deleting a client therefore skips the `ClientRemovedEvent` branch, and this PR adds no V2 cleanup for the per-client resources and policies stored in the admin-permissions resource server. Those authorization records remain after the target client is gone; add V2-specific cleanup for deleted clients.
